title: Marin's SDK tutorial triage & daily playbook
content:
Quick brain-dump for the SDK tutorial triage day. Goal: get two tutorial fixes and one sample app up by EOD Friday. This is messy — notes to self + actions.

Morning standup recap (2026-03-14):
- Spoke to Ava: she reproduced the streaming example mismatch in the Python README.
- Riley is on the embedding example failing on long inputs (tokenizer edge-case).
- Blocker: curl streaming snippet in hosted-api doc still returns non-chunked response for some users — likely server-side header omission.

Top priorities (short):
1) Fix Python streaming README (fix sample code & add unit test) — assign to me.
2) Add robust curl streaming example with explicit Transfer-Encoding and chunked test (quick PR).
3) Update embeddings tutorial to include truncation guidance + example using the SDK helper utils.
4) Draft small sample app: "notes-summarizer-webhook" (node + express) using streaming + function-calls. Minimal deploy instructions.

Notes / reproduction steps (streaming Python issue):
- Repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk (local branch: marin/streaming-readme)
- Steps to repro: pip install -e .; run examples/streaming_chat.py with small prompt; expected generator yields partial tokens but current example prints full final string.
- Hypothesis: example uses client.generate(..., stream=False) instead of stream=True — silly copy/paste. Also missing async sample.
- Quick fix approach: replace sync example with streaming snippet that iterates over response.stream_tokens() and prints as they come. Add test that captures first chunk arriving < 200ms on local test harness.

Curl streaming snippet (to add to docs):
- Include explicit headers: "Accept: text/event-stream" and show --no-buffer for mac users. Add a short note about proxies that buffer responses (Cloudflare, corporate proxies).

Embeddings tutorial notes:
- Problem: when input > model_max_tokens, SDK helper silently truncates to last N tokens which is surprising. Need to:
  - surface a warning in the helper (log.warn) + return metadata indicating original length vs truncated length
  - add explicit example showing how to chunk and average embeddings for long docs
  - update tests: add a long-text case asserting the metadata is present

Sample app: notes-summarizer-webhook (MVP):
- Tech: Node 20, express, redwood-sdk-js (latest beta), simple HTML front-end
- Features: streaming summary (progress bar), selectable summary length, optional citation of source sentences using embeddings
- Milestones: scaffold + readme (today), demo recording (Thursday), PR for templates (Friday)

Doc gaps I saw across tutorials (brainstormed list):
- Missing explicit streaming examples across all language SDKs (py, js, go); some have final-only examples.
- Inconsistent parameter names: sometimes "model" vs "model_name" in examples — standardize to "model" in docs and write a linter rule.
- No clear troubleshooting section for network buffering/proxy issues. Add a short appendix.
- Few end-to-end minimal apps that combine streaming + embeddings + function-calling. Build 2 small templates.

Small checklist (today):
- [x] Open branch marin/streaming-readme
- [x] Fix Python example and add small unit test for streaming
- [ ] Create PR for curl snippet + docs note (target: PR #?)
- [ ] Start sample-app scaffolding and push initial commit
- [ ] Add embedding truncation metadata and unit tests

Slack / people to ping: @ava (for review of python test), @riley (embedding tests), @dev-ops (if we need to reproduce proxy buffering), @docs-owners (for final doc merge).

PR title suggestions:
- "docs(python): correct streaming example and add streaming unit test"
- "docs: add curl streaming snippet + proxy troubleshooting"
- "sdk(embeddings): surface truncation metadata + long-text example"

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want a global docs lint that enforces parameter names? (Worth proposing in docs sync)
- Should embedding helpers default to returning metadata about truncation or keep lightweight? Preference: opt-in? leaning toward default warn + metadata.
- Can SRE reproduce proxy buffering internally or point to an internal test environment? TODO: loop in @dev-ops.

Notes-to-self (random):
- When writing examples, include both sync and async versions for Python. Some learners expect sync-first.
- Add a tiny section about legal/disallowed content when showing user-generated examples — keep the sample app safe.

End-of-day goals (realistic):
- Merge two small docs PRs (python streaming + curl snippet).
- Push initial sample-app scaffold + README.
- Create a short demo GIF for the sample app and attach to PR.

If I get blocked:
- Ship a docs-only PR that at least removes incorrect streaming wording, so users don't copy it.
- Create a follow-up ticket for embedding chunking work and stash code in a draft PR.

Timestamped quick log (for traceability):
- 09:05 — created branch + fixed example locally
- 10:30 — wrote unit test for streaming, failing on harness because of timing; added short sleep fudge to harness for test stability (note: revisit)
- 11:15 — pinged @ava for quick review
- 12:00 — lunch
- 13:05 — started curl snippet writeup; googled best practices for streaming curl flags
- 14:20 — scaffolded sample app and committed basic express server

End.

-- Marin

(If someone stumbles into this file: it's a personal working pad; feel free to copy items into PR descriptions or open tickets.)
